title: Latino Voter Backlash Thwarts GOP Redistricting Push in South Texas
snippet: Texas Republicans' high-stakes bid to gain five congressional seats in the Rio Grande Valley backfired after Hispanic voters decisively rejected conservative economic and immigration policies.
content:
A high-stakes gamble by Texas Republicans to lock in control of the state's congressional delegation backfired on Election Day, as a surge in Latino turnout in South Texas dealt the GOP a major setback.

Hoping to build on President Donald Trump's 2024 gains among Hispanic voters, the Republican-controlled state legislature executed a controversial mid-decade redistricting effort aimed at picking up five additional U.S. House seats. The redistricting map heavily targeted four counties in the predominantly Latino Rio Grande Valley. However, Republicans failed to flip a single seat in the region—losing all four by double-digit margins—and ultimately suffered a net loss of one House seat overall.

Immigration Raids and Inflation Drive Voter Revolt

Data from the ABC News Voter Poll indicates that growing frustration over federal immigration enforcement and economic strain pushed South Texas voters back toward the Democratic column. In Texas, Hispanic voters represent more than 30% of the electorate and make up over 90% of the population in key Rio Grande Valley counties.

Severe immigration crackdowns deeply affected local communities, according to Jon Taylor, a political science professor at the University of Texas at San Antonio. Taylor noted that many residents in South Texas had relatives, friends, or acquaintances detained in recent ICE raids, creating a powerful motivation at the ballot box. Poll results revealed that 67% of Hispanic voters believed federal immigration enforcement had gone too far.

Economic discontent proved equally decisive in the working-class region. Roughly 83% of Hispanic voters characterized the economy as poor or not so good, with 75% stating that federal economic policies had exacerbated financial pressures in their daily lives. Advocates noted that the high poverty rates in the Rio Grande Valley made working families particularly vulnerable to rising costs.

Democrats Sweep Statewide Races as Turnout Soars

Driven by voter mobilization, turnout across the Rio Grande Valley rose significantly compared to 2022 levels, outstripping the statewide average increase. Hidalgo County saw a nearly 10% jump in turnout, while Cameron, Willacy, and Starr counties also posted notable gains.

The momentum helped propel Democrats to victory across all statewide contests. Senate candidate James Talarico secured 68% of the Hispanic vote statewide, while gubernatorial candidate Gina Hinojosa won 65%. Democrats also managed to flip two South Texas congressional districts previously carried by Trump by double digits.

Latino political advocacy leaders argue the election results signal a turning point for the state's political landscape, demonstrating that future presidential hopefuls cannot afford to overlook the political power of Hispanic voters in Texas.
